concept.name: Trend day
concept.definition: A Market Profile day type dominated from the open by longer-timeframe participants on one side: the initial balance is narrow, price extends the range repeatedly in one direction (one-time-framing, with successive brackets making higher highs or lower lows), and the profile is elongated and thin rather than bell-shaped. It is a structural description of strong directional conviction.
concept.intuition: On a trend day the market picks a direction early and never looks back — every rotation is shallow, and the close comes near the day's extreme.
concept.mechanics: Recognized by a narrow initial balance, one-sided range extensions, minimal overlap between successive brackets, a wide value area that keeps migrating in the trend direction, and excess (a single-print tail) at the day's final extreme.
concept.failure_modes: Trend days are only obvious late in the session; many days that begin as trend days fail into rotation, and counter-trend trades against a genuine trend day are among the costliest profile-reading errors.
concept.misconceptions: A big directional day is not automatically a trend day in the profile sense — the classification depends on structure (narrow IB, one-time-framing, elongated distribution), not just the size of the move.
concept.example: ES opens at 4,500, never trades back through the open, and each successive 30-minute bracket prints a higher high through a 60-point range; the profile closes near the high with a long thin shape — a textbook trend day.
